contests.title: Hall County schools — senior homestead exemption changes

provenance.sourceOrg: Office of the Governor of Georgia
provenance.quote: Shall the Act amending the existing senior citizen homestead exemption for Hall County school district ad valorem taxation for educational purposes be approved so as to increase the income cap on the first exemption provided to residents 62 years of age and older from $25,000.00 to $40,000.00 and to provide a new exemption for residents 66 years of age or older for the first $1,200,000.00 of the appraised value of the homestead?

measures.questionText: Shall the Act amending the existing senior citizen homestead exemption for Hall County school district ad valorem taxation for educational purposes be approved so as to increase the income cap on the first exemption provided to residents 62 years of age and older from $25,000.00 to $40,000.00 and to provide a new exemption for residents 66 years of age or older for the first $1,200,000.00 of the appraised value of the homestead?

provenance.sourceOrg: Office of the Governor of Georgia
provenance.quote: Shall the Act amending the existing senior citizen homestead exemption for Hall County school district ad valorem taxation for educational purposes be approved so as to increase the income cap on the first exemption provided to residents 62 years of age and older from $25,000.00 to $40,000.00 and to provide a new exemption for residents 66 years of age or older for the first $1,200,000.00 of the appraised value of the homestead?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raises the income limit from $25,000 to $40,000 for the existing $30,000 assessed-value school-tax homestead exemption for qualifying disabled residents or residents ages 62 through 65. The income limit counts the resident and a spouse living in the homestead for the preceding taxable year. It adds an exemption for up to $480,000 of assessed homestead value at age 66 or older; the ballot question describes this as the first $1.2 million of appraised value. Residents age 70 or older would continue to receive a full-value homestead exemption from these school taxes; ages are measured on January 1 of the year the relevant exemption is applied for or first claimed. Qualifying unremarried surviving spouses may retain the relevant exemption while continuing to occupy the home: age 55 or older for the income-limited $30,000 tier, age 66 or older for the $480,000 tier, and age 65 or older for the full-value tier. Recipients of the first tier would not need to reapply for the age-66 tier, and recipients of that tier would not need to reapply for the age-70 full-value tier. Assessed value above a partial exemption remains taxable; if voters approve, the changes take effect January 1, 2027.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the higher $40,000 income limit, new age-66 exemption and related eligibility and application changes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the proposed changes to the school-tax senior homestead exemptions.
